newsitem.title: UK: POLAND TO TENDER 39.94 PCT OF GDANSKI.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TO TENDER 39.94 PCT OF GDANSKI.

text.p: HSBC Investment Bank has released the Polish treasury from a lockup agreement under the terms of its issue of global depositary receipts, which prevented the state from selling further shares in the bank in the 12 months after its GDR issue.
The Polish treasury will now sell a 39.94 percent stake in Bank Gdanski via a public tender, said HSBC which was the lead manager of the bank's GDR issue.

"Following a formal request by the State Treasury of the Republic of Poland acting through the minister of finance, HSBC Investment Bank has consented to the release of the State Treasury from its undertaking not to dispose of any shares in Bank Gdanski before 18 December 1996," HSBC said.
No further details on the tender offer were available and it is not clear whether a further tranche of the bank will be sold overseas.
The Polish Treasury will retain a five percent stake in the bank.
